topic: How does defocused feed array placement optimize coverage versus scan loss in DBF architectures?
consensus_response: Defocused feed arrays minimize scan loss by strategically varying element spacing to achieve optimized beamforming patterns. This reduces interference from off-axis elements, leading to a focused signal path with lower path loss and reduced susceptibility to atmospheric turbulence and ground clutter.  This directly translates to increased network capacity and reduced link margin requirements, particularly in challenging environments.
reference_context: Defocused feed arrays offer robust performance against feed element failures by minimizing scan loss through precise beamforming. This minimizes signal attenuation caused by environmental stressors like atmospheric turbulence and ground clutter, leading to improved system resilience.
